data.name: Sling Ming
data.detailed_description:
"..sigh... Why do they always hide important keys in the farthest corners of the galaxy?"

Princess Ming is desperate to find the cause of the never-ending earthquakes that plague her kingdom. An old and mysterious door, deep below her castle, seems to hold the answer. The star coordinates next to the three giant locks is her only clue. Get the royal rocket ready!

The Oxylane


Hook up to the Oxylane, a transit system that lets you fly through the air, swing around corners and defy gravity.

  • Plan your path by arranging the Oxylane nodes
  • Time your moves to control your swing and perform cool aerials
  • Rearrange and revisit nodes to solve puzzles

The Story


Back in the days, before Ming became princess, the air was so polluted it was harmful to breathe. People hooked up to the Oxylane via elastic tubes to get fresh air. Over time it evolved into a standardized way of transportation. The daily commute to the coal mines and oil refineries would have been impossible without the Oxylane!

That all changed with the revolution and the Big Cleanup. But with the king missing and the kingdom plagued by earthquakes, are old sins really dead or just buried and forgotten?

Game Features

  • Mix of action and puzzles that rely on physics, timing or logic
  • Boss fights and unlockable abilities
  • Highscore and challenges on every level
  • Play with mouse or joypad (full controller support)
  • Characters and story that unveil as you progress
  • Beautiful worlds, amazing soundtrack and a big-hearted adventure!

reviews.review:
[h1]Sling Ming[/h1]

The earth rumbles with constant anger, and a revered Princess of some prosperous civilization has had her fill of the terror it causes her people. This princess, Ming, with the help of her trusty and long-serving assistant of many generations take up responsibility in place of their missing King and brave the toxic depths beneath their homeland to find the source. With the use of a trusty old oxygen suit used in olden days of her world to brave the polluted outside lands, Ming sets out on a tethered adventure of particular navigational spelunking.  

[i]Sling Ming[/i] is a beautiful and artistic world of cosmic regions and deathly omens of pollution, with an inventive and very unique mechanic of node-altering, on-rails adventuring and puzzle solving in the most unpredictable of locations.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

A very simple and seemingly casual mechanic, Ming takes to the cavernous tunnels beneath the earth on her trusty sling which acts as a conveyor with a grapple. A long stretch of wire continues along each level, and with a simple click of each consecutive node ahead on the wire Ming takes off to the next point. Clicking to each point with either your mouse or gamepad and watching the physics carry our adorable protagonist, spinning and twirling along with gravity, feels really good and is incredibly easy. Things soon get complicated though, and all forms of enemies, obstacles, and hazards block the defaulted route of Ming's sling line.

You really have to consider the angle with which you lower yourself into the cave, and later on even the timing. Simply pathing your sling rope out of the way of hazards like toxic waste or lava isn't enough, as Ming is the real hitbox here not the node you control and she dangles pretty low beneath the actual grapple point. The erratic ragdoll physics on Ming's body as she bumps and tussles around on the sling is also used to full effect here, with many corners and ledges needing to be swung around with full momentum of her body in order to avoid hazards like radioactive pools of waste. Planning your route and taking into consideration where Ming will be positioned and where her bouncy little body will fling itself from the movement of your sling is all part of the challenge and the fun here.

Coins also sit dangerously near hazards and edges of the stage beckoning real daredevils to try their luck and skim close as possible to obstacles, gaining that sweet bit of treasure as a reward. Later on different node types are introduced such as speedier zip-lines that propel you through impossible openings with a double-tap, and make the whole coin obtaining and goal completing routine much more interesting and creative. These become important later when individual stages you tackle will all have a plethora of challenges and side-objectives to complete in addition to reaching each end goal.

[h1]Visuals/Sound[/h1]

Sling Ming features some very high-quality art for a sidescrolling game of such a casual nature, with an almost hand-painted and personal touch to it. The environments have a wonderful range of interplanetary aesthetics, from the dark toxic caverns you start in to the gorgeously detailed lush and vibrantly green planet you take off to afterwards. Ming herself is of course super adorable, and all of the strange little alien critters you encounter and have to dodge are so imaginative in a cosmically extraterrestrial way, even in their personality and movement patterns. This has some of the most professional looking artwork I've seen in recent 2D games, and its something that needs to be seen in all of its smooth and charming animated glory to truly appreciate.

The music of your adventure is suitably ominous during the deep and dark spelunking into unknown caves and toxic underworlds, while appropriately whimsical on the climbs into the more vibrant and lush outside worlds. Its an impressive and memorable soundtrack with a wide range of instruments, including some pleasing Chinese fiddles and other cultural instrumentation thrown into the mix for that "Planetary" feel. Little bits of the dialogue come with short bits of voiced phrases, usually different humorous expressions from Ming and definitely serve to draw you into the story of global peril at the hands of pollution.

[h1]Final Thought[/h1]

Sling Ming has a brilliantly simple but very open-ended gameplay mechanic with a wealth of interesting possibilities for puzzles and physics challenges. Figuring out a proper path for you nodes is ultimately very satisfying, and watching Ming swing, bump, and bounce her way around the twisting mazes and obstacles is just plain fun. With the variation of different nodes and the types of movement they provide or alter, puzzles in the game are incredibly inventive and accessible, never tedious or overstaying their welcome. 

If you're looking for some unique and addictive indie action with a decent amount of fun-over-challenge kind of puzzles then absolutely give this a try. It's also absolutely freaking gorgeous.
